2610.13461.title: SqueezeBench: Saturation-Resilient Evaluation of Mathematical Capability
2610.13461.paper_summary: AI systems are making rapid progress in mathematics, but this progress is hard to measure. Benchmarks of solved problems saturate, and in benchmarks of open problems each problem can be resolved for the first time only once. We present SqueezeBench, a benchmark that is resilient to saturation: a success raises the bar instead of removing the problem. Each problem fixes an integer function $f(n)$ whose values are known only for small $n$, and the benchmark keeps a lower and an upper record on it. A record is a computable Lean function with a machine-checked proof that it bounds $f$. A submission proposes a new function and proves that it bounds $f$, that it is no worse than the current record at any $n$, and that it is strictly better at some $n$. Once accepted, it becomes the record that the next submission has to beat. The system thus chooses the bound as well as its proof, and it may improve the record at a single $n$ or its growth rate. At every $n$, the gap between the two records shows how far the certified bounds are from determining $f(n)$. Every proof is checked by two independent Lean kernels, so no referee needs to check the mathematics. The checks also reject a function that computes $f$ by exhaustive search at small $n$, and a maintainer only reads the submitter's report and looks for such a search at larger $n$. We release ten problems from extremal combinatorics with twenty proved initial records and the admission tools. As a baseline, agents based on a frontier language model, with at most one hour per record, had 82 submissions accepted and improved every record, without going beyond the published literature. Agents based on two newer models then started from these records, had 60 more submissions accepted and improved 19 of the 20 records again. For eight of the ten problems, at least one record is still asymptotically behind the best published bound.
2610.13461.paper_summary_zh: AI 系統在數學領域取得了快速進展，但這種進展難以衡量。解決問題的基準已經飽和，而在開放問題的基準中，每個問題只能首次解決一次。我們提出了 SqueezeBench，一個對飽和具有韌性的基準：成功會提高標準，而不是移除問題。每個問題固定一個整數函數 $f(n)$，其值僅對小的 $n$ 已知，基準保持對其的下限和上限記錄。記錄是一個可計算的 Lean 函數，並附有機器檢查的證明，證明它界定了 $f$。提交的內容提出一個新函數，並證明它界定了 $f$，在任何 $n$ 上不比當前記錄差，並且在某些 $n$ 上是更好的。一旦被接受，它就成為下一個提交需要超越的記錄。因此，系統選擇界限及其證明，並可能在單個 $n$ 或其增長率上改進記錄。在每個 $n$ 上，兩個記錄之間的差距顯示經過認證的界限距離確定 $f(n)$ 還有多遠。每個證明都由兩個獨立的 Lean 核心檢查，因此不需要裁判檢查數學。檢查還會拒絕通過小的 $n$ 進行全面搜索來計算 $f$ 的函數，維護者僅閱讀提交者的報告，並尋找在更大 $n$ 上的此類搜索。我們釋放了來自極端組合學的十個問題，並提供了二十個已證明的初始記錄和入場工具。作為基準，基於前沿語言模型的代理，每個記錄最多一小時，接受了 82 次提交並改進了每個記錄，沒有超越已發表的文獻。然後，基於兩個更新模型的代理從這些記錄開始，接受了 60 次更多提交，並再次改進了 20 個記錄中的 19 個。對於十個問題中的八個，至少有一個記錄仍然在漸進上落後於最佳發表的界限。
